name: AntiLife
blurb: Conway's Life in negative: swap live and dead and every Life pattern behaves the same.

name: InverseLife
author: Jason Rampe
blurb: Has Life-like gliders and oscillators. It is B3678/S23 with live and dead swapped.
Strobing; spearheaders grow out of its chaotic, oscillating pattern edges.

name: Wickstretcher And The Parasites
blurb: Explosive and strobing. Wickstretchers of many speeds and sizes appear, most with parasites clinging on that resize their wicks.

name: Oils
blurb: Explosive; full of wickstretchers, and home to a diagonal c/16 spaceship.

name: Invertamaze
blurb: Builds mazes that swap live and dead on every step. Warning: rapid flashing.

name: Neon Blobs
blurb: Strobing; patterns blow up into glowing, neon-looking blobs.

name: H-trees
blurb: Explosive growth of branching H shapes along the edges of patterns.

name: Fuzz
blurb: Explosive, with solid regions forming in the growth.

name: Gnarl
author: Kellie Evans
blurb: Explosive: one live cell is enough to grow an intricate, gnarled pattern.

name: Snakeskin
blurb: Explosive; the growth fills with snake-like shapes.

name: Solid islands grow amongst static
blurb: Grows rapidly; solid islands form inside regions of static-like noise.

name: Replicator
blurb: Any pattern at all makes copies of itself.

name: Fredkin
blurb: Like Replicator, any pattern copies itself. Also called Replicator 2.

name: Feux
blurb: Explosive; patterns become replicators that blink on and off.

name: Forrest of Ls
blurb: Explosive, though the inside of the growth slowly settles into still shapes.

name: Seeds
author: Brian Silverman
blurb: No cell survives a step, yet it explodes. Many small orthogonal spaceships, but most patterns blow up.

name: Live Free or Die
blurb: Explosive; only isolated cells survive. Rich in oscillators, spaceships and puffers, some stretchable to any size and period.
Explosive; a replicator exists, which is rare among B2 rules.
Explosive, but some still lifes are permanent walls; used as casings, they guide one-shot signals and allow logic gates.
Behaves much like B2/S2345.
Behaves much like B2/S2345.

name: Serviettes
blurb: Like Seeds, no cell survives and growth explodes, weaving patterns that look like fabric. Also called Persian Rug.
Explosive; home to an asymmetric replicator that copies along a single line.

name: Iceballs
blurb: Small solid clumps blink on and off; a few grow big enough to start spreading slowly. Also called Ice nine.

name: Life without death
blurb: Cells never die, so growth only spreads, forming intricate flakes and dense ladder wickstretchers. Also called Flakes or Inkspot.

name: DotLife
blurb: Life plus survival with zero neighbours; explosive. The B-heptomino often grows forever here, but it can be tamed into a spaceship.

name: Star Trek
blurb: Has spaceships moving at several different speeds.

name: Flock
blurb: Soups quickly reduce to period-2 oscillators, dominoes and duoplets; a period-14 pre-beehive shuttle is common.

name: Mazectric
blurb: Grows into mazes, like Maze, but with straighter, longer corridors.

name: Maze
blurb: Spreads and hardens into a maze of corridors.

name: Magnezones
blurb: Explosive, with a fluid-like interior in which four kinds of crystal form.

name: Corrosion of Conformity
blurb: Mazectric without S3. Nearly any start burns slowly, eating away at its surroundings like rust.

name: EightFlock
blurb: Flock with survival on 8 added.

name: LowLife
blurb: Life with survival on 1 instead of 2.
Just six still lifes up to 8 cells and none from 9 to 19; common oscillators include the blinker and toad.

name: Conway's Life
author: John Conway
blurb: The most famous and most studied Life-like rule; chaotic, with endlessly complex behaviour.

name: EightLife
blurb: Life with survival on 8 too. Also called Pulsar Life.

name: Shoots and Roots
blurb: Two kinds of growth: orderly, slow shoots and faster, explosive roots.

name: Coral
blurb: Slow, explosive growth with a texture like coral.

name: 3-4 Life
blurb: Long thought a stable cousin of Life, until computers showed most patterns explode. Many tiny oscillators; period-3 ships move straight and diagonally.

name: Never happy
blurb: Explosive but sluggish; growth takes on diamond outlines.

name: Assimilation
blurb: Very stable; growth ends in lasting diamonds, part-filled inside. As in 2x2, block patterns always stay block patterns.

name: Long Life
blurb: Stable, and named for its many simple oscillators with extremely long periods.

name: Spiral and polygonal growth
blurb: Plows crawl along polygon edges, enlarging them and turning corners. One 16-cell methuselah runs 12127116559 generations before settling to period 2.

name: Gems
blurb: Explosive, with many small oscillators of high period and a very slow c/5648 spaceship.

name: Gems Minor
blurb: Like Gems: explosive, with plenty of small oscillators of high period and a slow c/2068 ship.

name: Grounded Life
blurb: Stable; Life plus birth on 5. Life's usual ships fail, and the commonest ship is Glider 3736, orthogonal at 2c/5.

name: Land Rush
blurb: Chaotic growth spreads out and sorts itself into rows like ploughed fields.

name: Eppstein
author: Dean Hickerson and David Eppstein
blurb: Explosive; Life plus birth on 5 and survival on 6.

name: Bugs
blurb: Explosive, with lots of spaceships packed with live cells.

name: Cheerios
blurb: Explosive; objects called cheerios appear amid the chaos.

name: Holstein
blurb: Self-complementary. Froth wears solid regions away from the corners unless edge oscillators hold them. Ships at c/7, c/5, c/4 and c/3.

name: Diamoeba
blurb: Grows big diamonds whose edges churn chaotically; some patterns grow quadratically, and block patterns stay block patterns, as in 2x2.

name: Amoeba
blurb: Chaotic and evenly poised between growth and decay: blobs with turbulent insides and edges that lurch about.

name: Pseudo Life
blurb: Soups look much like Life's, but the glider breaks down, so few Life patterns carry over.

name: Geology
blurb: Chaotic and finely balanced: large live continents in a sea of roughly 50% chaos slowly wear down into islands. Self-complementary.

name: HighFlock
blurb: Flock with an extra birth on 6.
Chaotic, with many simple oscillators, still lifes and ships. The name: any pattern built of 2x2 blocks stays built of 2x2 blocks.

name: IronFlock
blurb: Flock with birth on 6 and survival on 8 added.

name: HighLife
blurb: Life plus birth on 6. Behaves much like Life, but famous for a small replicator.

name: Land Rush 2
blurb: Explosive; once mixed up with Land Rush, probably through a typo. Has an orthogonal c/2 ship of period 4.

name: Virus
blurb: Explosive. The T-tetromino becomes a puffer that leaves blinkers behind, a fitting echo of its traffic-light fate in Life.

name: IronLife
blurb: HighLife with survival on 8 added.

name: sqrt replicator rule
blurb: Has a messy orthogonal replicator, hence the name; once called the logarithmic replicator rule.

name: DrighLife
blurb: Life plus births on 6 and 7: the HighLife and DryLife changes together.
2x2 with births on 7 and 8 and survival on 8 added.

name: Castles
blurb: Patterns nearly explode before freezing into stable, castle-like forms.
Life plus births on 6, 7 and 8; InverseLife with live and dead swapped.

name: Stains
blurb: Stable: most patterns fill in the areas they enclose. Nearby rules, Coagulations among them, usually explode.

name: Day & Night
blurb: Stable and self-complementary: live and dead regions follow the same law. Many patterns with intricate behaviour are known.

name: LowDeath without Death
blurb: LowDeath in which cells never die.
Explosive, behaving like 2x2. Its tiny 4c/13o replicator has been used to build W110 unit cells and guns.

name: Life SkyHigh
blurb: HighLife plus B8 and S6, which explains the name.

name: LowDeath
blurb: HighLife's replicator still works, though it runs a different sequence because of the pedestrian effect of B38/S23.

name: Morley
blurb: Random soups settle very fast. A slow spaceship and a slow puffer are both common. Also called Move.

name: DryLife without Death
blurb: Cells never die, as in Life without death, but growth goes quadratic instead of building ladders.

name: DryFlock
blurb: Flock with an extra birth on 7.

name: Mazectric with Mice
blurb: Mazectric plus B7; mice shuttle to and fro along the maze corridors.

name: Maze with Mice
blurb: Maze plus B7. As in Mazectric with Mice, mice shuttle along corridors that keep lengthening.

name: DryLife
blurb: Life plus B7; explosive. Ships larger than the glider fail, hence the name. A 9c/28 R-pentomino puffer can be combined into spaceships.

name: Plow World
blurb: Explosive; cells never die, and some patterns become wickstretchers.

name: Coagulations
blurb: Explosive; patterns usually spread without end, leaving thick goo. Oddly, it has one birth condition fewer than the stable Stains.

name: Pedestrian Life without Death
blurb: Pedestrian Life in which cells never die.

name: Pedestrian Flock
blurb: Pedestrian Life's births (3 and 8) with Flock's survival (1 and 2).

name: HoneyFlock
blurb: Flock with the extra B8 and S8 that HoneyLife adds to Life.

name: Pedestrian Life
blurb: Life plus birth on 8, with growth patterns all its own and oblique (5,2)c/190 spaceships.

name: HoneyLife
blurb: Pedestrian Life's B8 together with EightLife's S8, both added to Life.

name: Electrified Maze
blurb: Maze with birth on 4 and 5 instead of 3.

name: Oscillators Rule
blurb: Soups dwindle to tiny oscillators and still lifes; periods above 16 are rare.

name: Walled cities
author: David Macfarlane
blurb: Stable; pockets of seemingly random activity sit inside walls that keep them apart.

name: Vote 4/5
blurb: A twist on Gérard Vichniac's voting rule that models majority opinion; also called Anneal.

name: Rings 'n' Slugs
blurb: Activity settles down into the stable rings and slugs that give the rule its name.

name: Vote
author: Gérard Vichniac
blurb: Each cell takes the majority state of its 3x3 block, a simple model of voting. Also called Majority.

name: 9:43 at Knight
author: EricG
blurb: A stable four-state Generations rule.

name: Banners
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Explosive; ships often trail banners that lengthen and flutter.

name: BelZhab
blurb: Explosive; shows Belousov-Zhabotinsky-style reaction patterns.

name: BelZhab Sediment
author: Jason Rampe
blurb: Explosive; BelZhab-style activity that leaves spreading beds of sediment.

name: Bloomerang
author: John Elliott
blurb: Expanding waves bounce back into slow, soft, rounded kaleidoscopic forms.

name: Bombers
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Chaotic; a close cousin of Star Wars with many more decay states, full of fine oscillators, ships and puffers.

name: Brain 6
author: Michael Sweney
blurb: Chaotic; a variant of Brian's Brain for which many patterns have been built.

name: Brian's Brain
author: Brian Silverman
blurb: Chaotic and widely loved: a ready cell fires when exactly two neighbours fire, then rests for a step. Nicknamed Brain or BB.

name: Burst
author: Michael Sweney
blurb: Chaotic; kin to Nova and Prairie on fire. Big regions slowly fade or break into oscillators; named for a typical exploding oscillator.

name: Burst II
author: Michael Sweney
blurb: Chaotic; Burst minus its one-cell still life (no S0). Has ships fast and slow, methuselahs, and a signature oscillator of period 500+.

name: Caterpillars
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Chaotic, and full of objects that look like caterpillars.

name: Chenille
blurb: An explosive six-state Generations rule.

name: Circuit Genesis
author: Charles A. Rockafellor
blurb: Expanding; grows circuit-like structures that keep developing long after the starting pattern's edges have moved away.

name: Cooties
author: Rudy Rucker
blurb: Explosive and lively; cells swarm about like lice.

name: Ebb and Flow
author: Michael Sweney
blurb: Slowly explosive, with lively motion inside the growing edge. A pattern's symmetry often decides whether it grows forever or dies.

name: Ebb and Flow II
author: Michael Sweney
blurb: Explosive; a near relative of Ebb and Flow, with simple gliders.

name: Faders
author: Rudy Rucker and John Walker
blurb: Explosive; part Life, part Brian's Brain. Cells are born and keep firing on exactly two firing neighbours, then fade through 23 refractory states.

name: Fireworks
author: John Elliott
blurb: Explosive; looks remarkably like fireworks. Random or designed starts both work, and even a few scattered cells run for a long time.

name: Flaming Starbows
author: Charles A. Rockafellor
blurb: Explosive; growing diamonds and skewed parallelograms sweep the grid, trailing fire and spirals, a bit like Faders crossed with Zhabotinsky spirals.

name: Frogs
author: Scott Robert Ladd
blurb: Chaotic; its frog-shaped gliders are very common and give it its name.

name: Frozen Spirals
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Cyclic; Zhabotinsky-style spirals whose corners grow icicles.

name: Glisserati
author: John Elliott
blurb: Explosive; simple seeds tend to fill with gliders in kaleidoscopic patterns, though some runs stay sparse, like Transers, with very long transients.

name: Glissergy
author: John Elliott
blurb: Explosive; Glisserati with 5 states instead of 7. That makes it much busier: random and simple starts alike run for a long time.

name: Lava
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Expanding; patterns fill in, very slowly, with something like molten lava.

name: Lines
author: Anders Starmark
blurb: Stable; rapidly sorts itself into straight lines and separate areas of orthogonal hatching. Best from a 20%-dense disc of radius 40 or more.

name: Living On The Edge
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Highly chaotic; whether a pattern lasts or dies out is hard to predict. Also called LOTE.

name: Meteor Guns
author: Charles A. Rockafellor
blurb: Expanding; most larger patterns become a slowly growing fireball that fires off gliders (the meteors). Still lifes and oscillators are easy to find.

name: Nova
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Expanding; solid seeds stream outward in steady, vivid growth whose border geometry depends on the seed's size and shape.

name: OrthoGo
author: John Elliott
blurb: Mostly quiet; glider collisions that spawn orthogonal products arise by themselves.

name: Prairie on fire
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Explosive; fire spreads across the grid. Looks best in reds and yellows.

name: RainZha
author: Rudy Rucker and John Walker
blurb: Explosive; about as simple as a Zhabotinsky-style rule gets. Random starts grow spirals by themselves.

name: Rake
author: Brian Prentice
blurb: Explosive; a Worms variant teeming with rake puffers, ships and growing wings. Collide them to build puffers and ships of any complexity.

name: SediMental
author: John Elliott
blurb: A 30% random fill forms stable islands with busy coasts and traffic between them; sparser starts stay thin, denser ones merge into one continent.

name: Snake
author: Brian Prentice
blurb: Explosive Worms variant. Its 3x3 square and shuttle oscillators combine into many more; a puffer laying shuttles leaves a snake-like tail.

name: Soft Freeze
author: John Elliott
blurb: Chaotic, on the edge between frozen and fluid: crystals grow, melt and regrow next to an active phase, seemingly without end.

name: Spirals
blurb: Explosive; steady spirals keep unwinding without end.

name: Star Wars
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Explosive; Brian's Brain with added stability, playing out like a space battle. Rich in natural glider guns. Also called MirekGro.

name: Sticks
author: Rudy Rucker
blurb: Explosive; ships drift among a growing collection of sticks.

name: Swirl
author: Scott Robert Ladd
blurb: Chaotic; separate whirlpools turn in empty space, in two usual sizes (swirlpool and flamewhirl), plus a flame glider whose twin tail flickers.

name: Thrill Grill
author: John Elliott
blurb: Expanding; glittering activity moves through and reshapes a grill of live cells.

name: Transers
author: John Elliott
blurb: Explosive and lively; many distinct objects arise naturally and change into one another.

name: Transers II
author: Michael Sweney
blurb: Explosive; Transers plus S0, with six states.

name: Wanderers
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Explosive; a near twin of Prairie on fire whose patterns roam about.

name: Worms
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: Explosive and vigorous; it breeds swarms of worms.

name: Xtasy
author: John Elliott
blurb: Explosive; in a closed grid, simple seeds make kaleidoscopic waves that dwell on X shapes.

name: Gnarl (LtL)
author: Kellie Evans
blurb: Explosive; the same rule as B1/S0V, written in LtL form.

name: Majority (LtL)
author: David Griffeath
blurb: Stable; each cell takes the majority of the 9x9 block around it.

name: Bosco's Rule
author: Kellie Evans
blurb: Chaotic; famous for its hollow spaceships, called bugs.

name: Waffle
author: Kellie Evans
blurb: An expanding range-7 rule.

name: Majorly
author: David Griffeath
blurb: Expanding; a range-7 rule whose thresholds amount to a majority vote over the 15x15 block.

name: Globe
author: Mirek Wójtowicz
blurb: An expanding range-8 rule.

name: Bugsmovie
author: David Griffeath
blurb: Chaotic; range 10. MCell calls it Bugs.

name: ModernArt
author: Charles A. Rockafellor
blurb: Chaotic; range 10 with 255 states.

name: Marine
author: MathAndCode
blurb: Chaotic; uses a custom HROT neighbourhood (N@03ddef) that JETCARP cannot run yet.

name: Factorio
author: H. H. P. M. P. Cole
blurb: Semi-stable; range 3 on a cross-shaped neighbourhood.

name: Coexistence
author: bubblegum
blurb: Chaotic; needs a weighted neighbourhood.

name: Hash
author: b-engine
blurb: Chaotic; uses the hash-shaped (#) neighbourhood.

name: Hexagonal Life
blurb: Life-like rule on hexagons: birth on 2, survival on 3 or 4.

name: Gnarl (von Neumann)
author: Kellie Evans
blurb: Gnarl on the four edge neighbours: born with one live neighbour, survives only with none.
